longQuestions: A file is a named collection of related data stored permanently on a secondary storage device (hard disk, USB) so that it remains after the program ends.

Types: (1) Text files — store data as readable ASCII characters in lines ending with newline; can be opened in a text editor (.txt). (2) Binary files — store data in the same binary form as in memory; not human-readable, but faster and more compact (.bin, .dat, images, executables).
By access, files may be sequential (read from start to end) or random-access (any record read directly using seekg/seekp).

Operations on files: (1) Creating/opening a file — open() or the stream constructor, e.g. ofstream f("data.txt"); (2) Writing data — using << or put()/write(); (3) Reading data — using >>, get(), getline() or read().

(4) Appending — adding data at the end with ios::app; (5) Searching/moving within the file — seekg(), seekp(), tellg(), tellp(); (6) Checking end of file — eof(); (7) Closing the file — close(); also deleting or renaming files (remove(), rename()).
A stream is a sequence (flow) of bytes between a program and an input/output device or file. C++ handles all I/O through streams.
Input stream — data flows from a source (keyboard or file) into the program; cin is the standard input stream (istream), and ifstream is used to read from files using >>, get(), getline().

Output stream — data flows from the program to a destination (screen, printer or file); cout is the standard output stream (ostream), and ofstream writes to files using <<, put(). fstream supports both input and output.
The mode of file opening specifies the purpose for which a file is opened (reading, writing, appending etc.); it is passed as the second argument of open(), e.g. f.open("a.txt", ios::out);

Modes: ios::in — open for reading; ios::out — open for writing (creates the file or erases old contents); ios::app — append, all output at the end; ios::ate — open and move to the end of file; ios::trunc — delete existing contents; ios::binary — open in binary mode; ios::nocreate / ios::noreplace (older compilers). Modes can be combined with |, e.g. ios::out | ios::binary.
File handling is the process of storing data in files and retrieving it using a program, so that data is kept permanently instead of being lost when the program ends.

In C++ it uses the header <fstream> with the classes ofstream (write), ifstream (read) and fstream (both). Steps: include <fstream> → create a stream object → open the file with a mode → read/write data → check errors/eof → close the file.
